question: What is the primary purpose of research dissemination in nursing?

options.A: To secure continuous funding from private agencies
options.B: To share study results so they can influence patient care and policy
options.C: To increase the personal academic rank of the principal investigator
options.D: To permanently archive data in university libraries

explanation: Research dissemination bridges the gap between research and practice by sharing study results to influence patient care, education, and health policy. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is dissemination considered an ethical responsibility toward study participants?

options.A: It ensures participants receive financial compensation for their time
options.B: It honors their contribution by translating their experiences into healthcare improvements
options.C: It guarantees that participants will not be contacted for future studies
options.D: It fulfills legal requirements to publish every master's thesis

explanation: Sharing study results honors the contribution of study participants by ensuring that the data they provided leads to tangible healthcare advancements. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is stakeholder identification crucial before disseminating research findings?

options.A: It ensures that the researcher receives financial grants before publication
options.B: It allows the researcher to tailor the messaging and format to the specific needs of the audience
options.C: It eliminates the need for statistical data analysis
options.D: It guarantees automatic approval from the ethical review board

explanation: Identifying stakeholders early helps researchers customize their language, format, and delivery to match the specific needs and literacy levels of each group. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h2)

question: When disseminating findings to a rural Nigerian community about sanitation, what is the best approach?

options.A: Use complex statistical models and medical jargon
options.B: Publish exclusively in international high-impact journals
options.C: Use simplified, culturally sensitive language adapted to local communication channels
options.D: Limit the dissemination strictly to hospital boardrooms

explanation: Community audiences require simplified, culturally sensitive communication in local languages or familiar dialects to ensure comprehension and practical application. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of relying solely on traditional academic journals for research dissemination?

options.A: It is too expensive for researchers to read their own published work
options.B: It often limits the reach of research, leaving frontline clinicians and community members uninformed
options.C: It does not undergo peer review before publication
options.D: It prevents academic promotion within universities

explanation: Traditional academic journals are often restricted by subscriptions and academic language, failing to reach frontline healthcare workers and the general public directly. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which dissemination format is most effective for quickly informing busy hospital management about new protocols?
explanation: Policy briefs provide concise, actionable summaries tailored for busy administrators and decision-makers who need quick insights for governance and planning. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the standard structure commonly used for writing empirical research papers in academic journals?
explanation: The IMRAD format (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion) is the universally accepted structural standard for peer-reviewed empirical research articles. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is a primary advantage of presenting research via a poster at a scientific conference?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any data analysis
options.B: It allows for direct, one-on-one networking and interactive feedback with peers
options.C: It guarantees immediate publication in a high-impact journal without review
options.D: It requires no preparation or financial investment

explanation: Poster presentations facilitate visual summarization and create opportunities for direct conversations, networking, and valuable feedback from fellow professionals. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of Knowledge Translation (KT) in nursing?

options.A: Translating academic papers from English to local Nigerian languages
options.B: Synthesizing, exchanging, and applying research findings to improve health outcomes
options.C: Converting handwritten patient notes into electronic medical records
options.D: Translating international nursing textbooks for classroom instruction only

explanation: Knowledge translation focuses on actively moving research evidence into real-world clinical practice and public health policies to improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does implementation science assist nurses in clinical practice?

options.A: It helps nurses design new laboratory equipment
options.B: It provides frameworks to study how evidence-based interventions are adopted in real-world settings
options.C: It calculates hospital budgets and nurse salaries
options.D: It replaces clinical judgment with automated computer algorithms

explanation: Implementation science studies how evidence-based practices are successfully integrated into routine clinical workflows and helps address real-world barriers. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a major financial barrier for researchers publishing in many international journals?

options.A: Mandatory travel expenses to conference venues
options.C: High costs of purchasing statistical software licenses
options.D: Mandatory fees for ethical board approval

explanation: High Article Processing Charges (APCs) charged by many open-access journals represent a significant financial hurdle for researchers in resource-limited settings. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h6)

question: How can nursing researchers help overcome institutional and writing barriers?

options.A: By working entirely in isolation without peer collaboration
options.B: By participating in mentorship programs and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams
options.C: By ignoring peer review feedback completely
options.D: By abandoning all quantitative research methods

explanation: Mentorship programs and multidisciplinary collaborations help build academic writing skills, share workloads, and overcome institutional hurdles. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is a key difference between traditional academic metrics and comprehensive research impact evaluation?

options.A: Traditional metrics focus only on citations, whereas comprehensive evaluation assesses real-world clinical and policy outcomes
options.B: Traditional metrics evaluate patient satisfaction, whereas comprehensive metrics evaluate only journal sales
options.C: Traditional metrics are used exclusively in nursing, while comprehensive evaluation is used only in physics
options.D: Traditional metrics require no data, while comprehensive evaluation requires no statistics

explanation: While traditional metrics measure academic citations, comprehensive research impact looks at practical, real-world changes in healthcare delivery and policy. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is evaluating the impact of disseminated research important for Nigerian nurse researchers?

options.A: It automatically guarantees a promotion to professor
options.B: It justifies funding investments and demonstrates accountability to stakeholders and communities
options.C: It removes the need for future ethical reviews
options.D: It prevents any future manuscript rejections

explanation: Evaluating impact shows accountability, justifies research funding, and provides valuable feedback on how to improve future healthcare interventions. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h7)
